about: What a GuestTest2 cell's key covers (contract 1.4, 2.1). keys.py reads it: entries[GUEST] merges over kinds[its kind], lists adding up. A kind says how the guest is reached: ssh (vm-update --try), probe (no --try: vm-update --probe), redox and sculpt (no SSH: a console probe). checks is what the judge reads, and keyed as a judge input; the rest (ram_gib, cpus, memory, timeout_s, update) is the runner's. S-*, L-*, K-*, B-* and M-* are guest_judge.py's rule codes. Not in guest: keys: update/trim.sh, update/pkgset.sh, update/fingerprint.py, holttest1d/judge.py (contract D2). sculpt2610 has no SSH: its no-ssh file (written by make-sculpt.sh) makes vm-update refuse it, and testvm/sculpt-update updates it offline, recording image-state, so its generation keys its cells as any guest's does; an update round runs sculpt-update for it (guest/update-sculpt.sh, mode console-update), which boots the update before it merges, so no --try PASS gates it in a bare round. vm-update keys as pycode: (keys.python_code: less its comments and docstrings, which only --help reads), so a comment or help-text change re-tests no guest; vm-mount and vm-umount key only the Linux guests (plats), since vm-update runs them only on a guest whose uname -s is Linux (its host mount check).

K-none and B-none for now: GRUB boots the kernel from /gnu/store (no /boot/vmlinuz for K-deb's count) and Shepherd is an init boot-state.sh doesn't know (it would say init unknown); a K-guix rule and a shepherd arm are later work, and touch every ssh guest's harness.  established false until its first GuestTest2 run

The same updater and rules as guix15 (K-none, B-none: its notes say why).  established false until its first GuestTest2 run

truenas25.notes: docs/design/truenas.md: TrueNAS CE 25.10; apt is off and no-vm-update refuses --try and the real update, so a probe boot only (vm-update --probe: check-image.sh before, no in-guest.sh); updates are rebuilds with a newer .update file (make-truenas.sh), staleness by testvm/truenas-update --check.  memory 4096: the middleware wants more than vm-run's 2048.  established true, as haiku6's: a probe never runs new-guest.sh

truenas25-mirror.notes: docs/design/truenas.md: TrueNAS CE 25.10, BIOS: boot-pool a two-disk mirror plus data pool tank on a third disk (vm-run-options --disk truenas25-mirror-b.qcow2 --disk truenas25-mirror-data.qcow2 --disk-serials BKOTN0,BKOTN1,BKOTN2); a probe boot only, as truenas25's (its notes say why); not in the vm-store, so only Chopin and Cinqcent hold it

uc24.notes: docs/design/ubuntu-core.md: Ubuntu Core 24, no TPM, not encrypted (vm-run-options --uefi --memory 2048); Linux.snapcore runs snapd's refresh and ends before Linux.common; snapd owns GRUB on ubuntu-boot (L-none, K-snapcore checks kernel.efi), there is no fstab of the four roots (M-none) and no apt source (S-none); established false until its first GuestTest2 run

void-zbm.notes: docs/design/zfsbootmenu.md: glibc Void on a ZFS root booted by ZFSBootMenu through its own NVRAM entry (vm-run-options --guest-vars uefi-vars.fd); L-zbm holds the ESP's EFI/ZBM images to the builder's (make-void-zfs.sh's zbm-kcl'd v3.1.0 release EFI, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-stamped), each boot environment's kernels and initramfs, BE void booted on its newest kernel, and hostid 00bab10c; kernels_max 3: two kernel series in BE void (linux and linux7.2), and vkpurge keeps the running one through an update

void-zbm-enc.notes: docs/design/zfsbootmenu.md: glibc Void on a ZFS root booted by ZFSBootMenu through its own NVRAM entry (vm-run-options --guest-vars uefi-vars.fd); L-zbm holds the ESP's EFI/ZBM images to the builder's (make-void-zfs.sh's zbm-kcl'd v3.1.0 release EFI, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-stamped), each boot environment's kernels and initramfs, BE void booted on its newest kernel, and hostid 00bab10c; kernels_max 3: two kernel series in BE void (linux and linux7.2), and vkpurge keeps the running one through an update; vm-update types vms/void-zbm-enc/zfs-passphrase at ZBM's prompt (its PROMPT pattern), and check-image.sh's read-only mount of BE void-6.18 needs zroot's key, loaded at boot
